summary: Seven public interest organizations protest MISO's large-load reliability filing, arguing its exemptions leave about 30 GW free of ramp and ride-through rules, that critical details sit in manuals, and that FERC should reject it.
ask: Reject MISO's Interconnection Reliability Requirements filing as not just and reasonable.

points.point: The organizations say the filing lets at least 30 GW of large load ramp fast and trip offline without limits.
points.quote: give at least 30 gigawatts (“GW”) of large load, though likely more, an unrestricted ability to ramp at eye-watering speeds and trip offline unexpectedly

points.point: MISO would fully exempt loads in service by December 4, 2026 and partly exempt loads tied to MTEP 2026 or EPR projects.
points.quote: large loads with a Service Commencement Date on or prior to December 4, 2026 will be entirely exempt from any reliability requirements

points.point: They say the exemptions go beyond the Show Cause Order and shift cost from large loads to other customers.
points.quote: MISO’s proposed exemptions go far beyond what the Commission’s Show Cause Order directed, represent a broad cost shift from large loads to other MISO customers

points.point: They cite a PJM event in which 3.8 GW of load tripped, about a tenth of the load MISO would exempt.
points.quote: PJM recently narrowly averted blackouts when 3.8 GW of load–a mere tenth of the load MISO proposes to exempt–tripped offline instantaneously.

points.point: They argue MISO has not shown any study of the reliability effect of the exemptions.
points.quote: if MISO has conducted any studies or analysis of the reliability impact of its proposed exemptions.

points.point: They object that most critical restrictions sit in Business Practices Manuals, which limits enforcement.
points.quote: MISO proposes to put most of the critical restrictions of the IRR Filing in Business Practices Manuals (“BPMs”).

points.point: An attached declaration puts the exempt load near a quarter of MISO's current summer peak.
points.quote: This makes 30,000 MW more than 24% of MISO’s current peak summer demand, and 20% of MISO’s peak summer demand with the new large loads in-service.

throughLine.text: Protests MISO's first filing after the E-8 order as exceeding what that order directed and shifting reliability costs to other customers, the cost-shifting concern at the core of E-8.
